findings.claim: New `raceAbortSignals` import in the batch link risks aborting a whole batch when a single batched request is cancelled (semantics differ from `allAbortSignals`).
findings.rationale: `httpBatchLink` deliberately uses `allAbortSignals`, which only aborts the combined signal once *every* batched caller has aborted — otherwise one consumer unsubscribing would kill the in-flight request for all other procedures sharing the batch. `raceAbortSignals` (abort as soon as *any* signal aborts) has the opposite semantics. The import alone is not a bug, but wherever it is used in the rest of this file it must be for a per-request/timeout signal (e.g. combining the batch signal with an abort-on-timeout signal), not for combining the per-caller signals. Please confirm the call site; if it replaced `allAbortSignals` for the batched callers, this is a behavior regression that will surface as spurious `AbortError`s for unrelated queries in the same batch. Medium confidence — I can only see the import in this hunk.

findings.claim: `raceAbortSignals` must be exported from `../internals/signals`, and unused-import lint/`noUnusedLocals` will fail if it is not referenced.
findings.rationale: The hunk only adds the named import; if `raceAbortSignals` is not (yet) exported from `internals/signals` this is a compile error, and if the corresponding usage was not included in the change the TS `noUnusedLocals`/eslint no-unused-vars rules typically enabled in this repo will fail the build. Low confidence without seeing the rest of the file, but worth verifying since this is the only visible change.
